text:
Predicates:
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
Win(x, m) ::: x wins in superhero movie m.
SuperheroMovie(m) ::: m is a superhero movie.
NamedAfter(m, c) ::: superhero movie m is named after character c.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: y is the nemesis of x.
InMovie(c, m) ::: character c is in movie m.

Premises:
∀m (SuperheroMovie(m) → ∀x (GoodGuy(x) → Win(x, m))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x ∀y ((GoodGuy(x) ∧ ¬GoodGuy(y)) → (Fight(x, y) ∧ Fight(y, x))) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesisOfSirDigby) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀m ∀c (NamedAfter(m, c) → GoodGuy(c)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (Win(x, y) → ¬Win(y, x)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting does not win.
∀m ∀c (NamedAfter(m, c) → InMovie(c, m)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is in the movie.

Conclusion:
¬Win(nemesisOfSirDigby, surprisingAdventures) ::: Sir Digby's nemesis does not win.
